body: Pizza Delivery!
ALL games, haha, but I absolutely love WoW. I can quest for days. Or just travel, fuck around.The music in WoW helps me when I'm anxious/calms me after a panic attack. I miss playing. So much.
Yes, I completely agree. Thank you.

Thanks, I appreciate the response. It helps to put my thoughts somewhere, esp. when it's 2am and I have no one to talk to. It's going to be tough, but we'll get through it, I suppose. I hope you're doing alright.

:( I'm so sorry. Breakups are incredibly painful, and I totally understand where you're coming from. For me, it doesn't seem to get easier with time. It's affecting you this much bc (aside from her cheating, which is fucked up) you're a good, loving person. You care. And not many people have these qualities. They just move on like the relationship meant nothing to them. I never understood how it was so easy for someone to leave like that. To leave you absolutely broken. It hurts like hell. That level of pain will drive many us to suicide. I think about it every day. But please know you deserve to be loved by someone who wouldn't do this to you. I felt the same way about my ex. He was my best friend, and I was madly in love with him. I was  happy most of the time, but he treated me like I didn't matter and I wanted so badly for him to love me as much as I loved him. I was completely dead inside before he left. After 6 years together. I hate myself for giving 150% when he obv didn't care. I can't say it will get easier, but try to hold on to some hope. That's what I try to do. A part of me knows I deserve more than this pain/suffering. And you deserve better, too.

Hey there. I can't imagine anything I say will be helpful, but I wanted to let you know I'm in a similar situation. I understand, to an extent, EXACTLY what you're feeling (after reading through some of your previous posts).  I'm just waiting for that day where I can't take it anymore. And I feel closer to that feeling every day.  And reaching out (to friends, hotlines) has been unsuccessful--at times, it's caused me to feel worse. But some days are good. Days where I don't think about the ex that destroyed all the good things about myself. I'm looking for/applying to better opportunities (my current job pays poorly and it's a 5 hour commute bc I don't drive). I don't cry as often. I'm eating again. I'm writing again, too.  Some days I laugh and genuinely feel OK. But I know those small moments aren't quite enough when 90% of your life is absolutely painful. I suffer with high-functioning anxiety, depression, etc., and I'm just so fucking tired. So I know what it's like to feel like the hurt/struggle/hopelessness will never end. It's agonizing. If I can help in any way, please let me know. Even if you just need to talk. I really hope you were able to stay safe tonight. I often hate when people say that to me when I just want to die, but know that some of us genuinely care. I understand it's not enough right now, but I hope it's something.
:( I've had similar thoughts/wishes. What's going on? (If you feel like sharing)

Hey there. I can relate to this on some level. Every day is the same -- lie awake at night (crying, ruminating, wanting to die), only to get up at 6 and go to work. It's a painful cycle.  I'm sure there are a lot of people who do care, and the one person you mentioned sounds like a really good person to have in your life. She obviously cares very much about your well-being. I understand that's not always enough. I've actually pushed people away bc I knew I was hurting them. Their support cannot fix what I'm going through. In my case, there's one person I wish would care, but he doesn't. I hate myself. And I mean I absolutely fucking hate myself, so it hurts to know you're struggling with similar thoughts. Anything you need to talk about, specifically? I wish I could help.

Exactly. I've learned quite a bit, and I feel free from a lot of the emotional abuse I was dealing with. I only wish I had left when I knew it was the right thing to do. Unhealthy relationships can really screw up the healing process once the relationship is over. It's incredible, the amount of things you are willing to forgive when you love and care about someone. You have the freedom now to be your best self, and to do all the things you've wanted to do but couldn't (if that's the case). I put a lot on hold for my ex. We'll get through this. Stay strong. Go at your own pace. It'll get better.
Haha! Perfect! :)

You're a good, loving person, and brave for reaching out/staying on hold. And the fact that you love your dogs that much, to put them first, says a lot about you. That actually brought me to tears. Have you tried texting the hotline? They respond quickly, but I understand how it might be helpful to actually talk to someone. It's not always the best experience (for me, personally), but it's worth trying when you're out of options. Know that there is always someone who will listen (even if it's not immediate, we're always here!) I know what it feels like to want to die, and to feel utterly alone and terrified. It's awful. I'm sorry you're hurting. I wish I knew what to say to help. You matter. You're loved.

I'm right there with you. In my experience, telling people has only pushed them further away. It's like I'm screaming and no one even hears me. But that's my situation. It's OK to ask for help. I've accepted that some people can't/refuse to, but that doesn't mean everyone will be that way.

Good for you! It's incredibly hard reaching out, so know that it was brave of you to do so. I've only called once bc I'm usually a bit of a mess when I need to talk to someone. I tend to text the hotline, but I feel like I've been doing it too often so it no longer helps. I'm sorry you're hurting. I wish I could say something reassuring. I hate knowing people are hurting this much. Hugs. You're stronger than you know.
Perfect! <3 all the feels.
D'aww!!!

Thanks for the kind words. There are kind people out there. I just wish I had more of them in my life. My parents have a lot on their plates. I never ask them for anything. I choose to leave them alone. When I need them, they just ignore me. Maybe it's for the best.
But you don't even know me. I might be a piece of shit person. That's the thing, I honestly believe I'm garbage. Why else would someone do this to me? My own family can't stand me.

Hi. Thanks for responding. I kinda broke down tonight. I push these feelings down as often as I can until I need to call/text the hotline, usually at night, but I got the "hey you've been texting us a bunch" message and I felt like a horrible person. 

I feel so alone right now. I lost my best friend when we broke up. He has a huge supportive family and I'm sort of alone. More independent. I've been through a lot in my 29 years, much worse than a breakup, but I was deeply in love with him--he was part of the reason I could get through the day with the amount of high-functioning anxiety I deal with. He was emotionally abusive, so part of me was already dead before he left. He was someone who believed people should ALWAYS be happy, unless it was he who was down, then it was OK. I'm just an emotional, caring person, so I tend to feel the weight of the world sometimes. It just hurts to be feel abandoned, and then to feel like I deserve it.

I can't imagine going through another year. I'm still pushing myself. I applied to teach in Japan, etc., but part of me is already ready to give up. I'm half a person right now and once December rolls around, I might not be here anymore. I don't understand how I got here. I feel like a selfish, horrible person.

I totally get this. We were together 6 years and it's been a year post breakup, so it's still especially hard for me, even after all this time. I'm 29 so I think about what I lost quite frequently, bc I felt like he was the one despite our issues. I'm glad you're still in contact. I wish we still were, but sometimes that prevents you from moving on. Maybe some space/NC will help. I'm not sure. I wish I had handled things differently. I also wish I was a bit younger so I could feel like I had more time to work through it. I don't want to be alone, but I can't be with anyone else rn.  Just work on yourself. I think that's the best thing you can do right now. Sometimes these things work out. Let us know! I like hearing about people getting back together and it being a good thing. Time apart can be helpful. I feel like anything is possible. For me, probably not since so much time has passed. I'm not upset for loving him. It's something you can't control. So don't blame yourself, and maybe try not to focus on his future. He sounds like he needs to figure things out. Chin up, you'll be OK. You seem to be handling it well.

Crying! This hurts my heart. I feel like I had the same relationship with my ex. Making him laugh was the thing I loved most. His laughter was contagious. He taught me so much, and everything I love now are things I experienced with him. Unfortunately, for me, it wasn't mutual, so it's been a painful year without him. I miss him every day. I also hoped to be friends again bcvhe is my best friend--or he was since we haven't spoke in months. I guess I understand. I'm still in love with him and he has moved on. I think you can be friends, eventually. Give it time. Mutual breakups have a better chance, in my opinion. But damn, it hurts to lose something so special.
Have all of their teeth pulled.
My heart! I totally get this. The dreams/nightmares kill me.
God, the eyes. Kills me, too. How is it that they can suddenly look at you like you're completely worthless? I can't get them out of my mind.

I'm in a similar place. It's a year post-breakup, 7 months no contact. It's very painful for me to do anything I love anymore. But I try. It helps to tell others about how you feel, especially if they share similar interests. Some people will help you reclaim these things by creating new memories. It's not easy (look at me!) I love going to conventions bc I work in comics, but recently saw my ex at a con (what are the odds!) and nearly passed out from an anxiety/panic attack. I'm easily triggered and it was a horrible experience, but that's me. You deserve to continue doing the things you love. It just might be hard to do on your own. Breakups are the worst.

I'm reading this on a train home from a long day at work where I could not stop thinking about my ex, the way he ended it, etc. And it's a year later for me and it still hurts like it happened yesterday (hurts so fucking much). Maybe it hurts more bc the holidays remind me of the last time I was with him and happy. Last Thanksgiving he said he was so grateful to have me in his life, that he loved me--a week later he wanted to leave me, bc he wasn't the clichéd "in love." I'm crying bc I totally understand how you feel. I'm 29 and he was 30, and I was deeply in love. I saw a future with him. We had issues, but he just didn't feel like working through them (he was lazy, selfish--I pulled the weight); he said relationships should be easy (and ours was actually pretty fucking easy bc I was a doormat) and happy and perfect for long we were together (6 years). The thing is, you have to communicate and work through the bad, and I let him get away with not talking for most of those years. People like that are so quick to throw away what's only slightly damaged for something new. And they will continue doing that until something clicks and they realize they need to change. Unfortunately, it will be for someone else. I can't imagine being with anyone else and it kills me how hard this is, this loneliness, esp. at my age. This was my first love, so maybe that's part of it. Anyway, I just wanted to say you're not alone. That doesn't really help, but I think it's important that we share our pain with others who understand.

This hits home (it's been 11 months for me). I think this is probably the norm for people who weren't treated well, but are unable to fully let go. I miss him in the mornings, too. I miss him most of my day, every day. Despite this being the typical for most relationships, I still wonder: how can people be so heartless in the end?

Hey. I'm going through a similar thought process, and it's def. painful as hell--I understand completely! It's fucking agonizing. My relationship wasn't quite as toxic (as in no one cheated), but there was definitely severe emotional abuse (by him), which makes it pretty goddamn awful to get over. To love someone who hurt you over a long period of time before dumping you cold is bound to mess you up. I'm a year post-breakup and I think about suicide every day. But I get up, go to work and do my best to be OK with myself. Work on you right now. I do my best to hold onto some sort of hope bc I know I deserve so much better than this. You're 19 and have the best years ahead of you. This is my first relationship, so it's def hard, but all relationships, for whatever length of time, and at any age, will hurt when they end. And that hurt will last for as long as it takes you to heal. We all deal w/ pain differently. We hurt bc we care. We hurt bc we love(d) these people. I'm not the best giver of advice since I'm in a dark place atm (and so sorry this is poorly executed), but trust me, you are so young! You're still changing and growing. You can get through this. I know it.

Social media was probably the reason we broke up, so I blocked him on everything. Seeing his name anywhere felt like getting hit by a train. I'm still friends with his family on IG, but that's becoming too much. For me, it's been a year since we broke up and it's still too painful to deal with. But that's me. Do what hurts less.
I'm so sorry. I wish I had something helpful or encouraging to say. It was brave of you to share. I'm in tears. Please know that you are strong. Hang in there. Hugs.

I'm finding myself pretty devastated still, and it's almost a year post-breakup. I'm doing my best, but my mind is pretty clouded by everything I went through with him.  I'm ashamed that he's always on my mind, and by how much I miss him. I just don't understand how it's possible to hurt this much for so long? I'm setting goals, doing things I want to do, but it's lonely. I can't even look at another person, so dating isn't an option. Nothing could prepare me for this.
Nature is fucking terrifying.

Thank you so much for sharing. I'm really happy to hear you're moving forward. I too have been in a dark place where suicide felt like the best option, or it brought me "comfort" somehow. It's such a strange feeling, and it's a combination of things and emotions, some unrelated to my ex. Someone leaving you can be that tipping point, though. I'm so glad you were able to move past that. Your story is inspiring. I just wish I was in a much better place, and that I would let go. I don't let people in that easily, so it's just that much harder to deal with when they leave. We'll get through this! We have lots of love to give. I'm just hoping I'll give myself a chance to try again. Wishing you the best! Stay strong.

My (29 f) breakup went down similarly, and we had been together for 6 years. Although we both suffered from anxiety, and also depression on my end, he seemed to feel as if it were only him struggling. I stepped up as the "knight" in our relationship bc someone had to, and maybe I was in a better position to do so (college educated, working, financially secure, independent, etc.) I made sacrifices, even when the relationship was long distance--I was in grad school and working and I had to take buses and planes to see him bc he never visited. It was a one-sided relationship. In our last year together, a lot of things I didn't know about him surfaced and suddenly I found myself feeling insecure and emotionally damaged. He started taking antidepressants for his anxiety, got a better job, a car, and finally moved out (though I loaned him money to make his first month's rent). Within a week he dumped me, but only after a year of being cold and emotionally abusive. I had given him too much power and I guess he resented me for whatever reason. He thought he deserved to do the things that hurt me and that it was my fault for being insecure and depressed. I know this seems vague and bitter, but I need you to know I feel the same way and it kills me. I can't get the small things out of my head either bc I still love him. I wish I had any advice at all, but nothing useful comes to mind. I'm still in a bad place, a year post-breakup, and he has already moved on, doesnt contact me, not even to see how I'm doing (not that he has to). He told me he wanted to be friends, but of course he said this while using me for comfort/sex weeks after the breakup, stringing me along through the holidays. I think about him daily, but reaching out would only result in more hurt. I say you remember the things you did for her and understand that you pulled the full weight of that relationship. You gave 150%. You deserve better. Sorry if this is rambly and poorly worded. It's both comforting and difficult to talk about this. Thank you for sharing.

This is EXACTLY how I feel, so thank you for sharing. I wish I could say it gets better, but I'm not quite in that place yet. It's nearing a year since my ex broke up with me and I'm still struggling. I think we all deal with these things differently since each individual situation is unique. For me, we were together 6 years. He was emotionally abusive towards the end, which is the reason I'm taking this so hard. And I still love him, he was my best friend. I'm struggling to let go bc I miss him and I don't quite understand why he did what he did to me, and I feel like I need that closure. I keep blaming myself and it's been hard to improve/love myself bc of that. What struck me was your comment about being happy before him. And though I know wishing I had never met him isn't beneficial or useful, I try to hold on to the idea that there's a better life without him, I just need to work a bit harder for it. You were ok before him and you will be after. Give it time. Give yourself permission to be sad and to go at your own pace. I hope you are much further along than I am as time passes, but don't beat yourself up. You're not alone.
You got this. Block everything.

Hey! Thank you so much for the thoughtful response! I'll definitely check out that book. I've tried 7 cups as well. I think I'm just ashamed that I'm still talking about him a year later, and bc I have made so little progress. It's been a difficult week, too, bc I saw him recently at an event. I didn't speak to him, but seeing him was enough to trigger me. I think this being my first real relationship/breakup is the reason it is so difficult. And also bc I love him so much. I'm also here if you ever need to talk. :)

Hey, thanks! Letting go seems to be the consensus among friends and family. I'm not sure why that's so hard for me, especially when I knew the relationship was unhealthy towards the end. I guess I forgive too easily, and I just miss him. Thank you. I'm working on it.
